Trap check: every headline number is a difference share, which equals the coverage RMS(r_eval - r_ref)/RMS(d) exactly (verified). None is a y_ref-fed output capacity. The report never calls a y_ref-fed capacity an H2 pass. However, its post hoc 'Gain ladder' table sets y_ref-fed conditional capacity against the frozen H2 values and 'H2 threshold 0.3', and says 'the ladder stays above 0.3'. Verdict reason (3) also argues from conditional capacity (0.415 vs H5 0.771; G7.5 0.310 vs 0.800). The identity baseline q = y_ref alone already gives 0.644 (gain median) and 0.471 (G7.5); for tone pairs it gives 0.164, and the y_ref-fed capacity is 0.046-0.058, which would trivially be below 0.3. The ladder should be labelled 'not an H2 quantity' and carry the identity baseline.

Oracles are labelled: repeat pairs are the floor, the G5 conditional capacity is omitted as an oracle, and conditional capacity is marked post hoc. The non-causal yfir_lead16 is labelled only implicitly ('lags -16..239' in variants, lead1:101; '16 lead taps' in the text). The word 'non-causal' never appears; recommend explicit labelling. No GPU and no model inference: the lead's cached CPU renders were used. Units: shares are RMS amplitude ratios. 'Error energy removed by delay' is a power ratio (ESR), consistent with the 79 % (power) in the lead's PREDICTION. The amplitude-vs-power trap was checked and did not fire. Sign convention of every lag estimator verified on synthetic device shifts of +2.0 and -0.95 samples (recovered to 1e-5). Reductions: frozen H5 recomputed on 3 pairs, x5_yh5 on 1 pair, identity on 3 pairs of one reference (ref 1); linearity measured for 2 of the 6 unmeasured variants. VS100R lags were run on all 12 runs x 4 takes on V, plus B for C and F3. The common-tau (bench-rule) stage was first started for C and F3 on a -5..+3 grid. I stopped that process myself (PID 1252239) after about 10 min (7.5 CPU-min) under load average about 22, and reran it reduced: F3 only, grid +-1 sample around each run's lag plus the grid edges. Its 4-take median ESR curve is sensitive to the take mix: for s43_r2 it gives tau +1.25 while the per-take optima are 0.90-1.39. Per-take ESR-optimal lags are therefore the primary numbers; the common-tau stage only illustrates the grid-edge consequence, which is robust for s44 (all takes 3.5-3.9 late) and not for s42. Runtime: stages nolly 2.2 min, identity 0.7 min, linearity 2.3 min, lags 6.9 min, common_tau reduced about 5 min; about 27 min of stage compute plus the stopped run, all CPU at 2 threads under nice 10. Nothing committed or staged; only files under diagnosis/probe_capacity/verify/ and tmp/probe_capacity/verify/ were written. The JSON also carries a short 'skeptic_summary' block.

claims_to_downgrade.claim: Verdict scope: 'a state or feedback beyond the probe memory (256 taps = 5.3 ms) cannot explain the H2 refusal'
claims_to_downgrade.reason: The bound uses only windows >= 30 ms (0.041). The same model-free measure just past the probe memory gives a larger share. Recomputed cold-start difference p1-p3, worst level, per gain take: 0.42 (G2.5), 0.40 (G5), 0.58 (G7.5), 0.39 (G10) in the first 1 ms frame after 256 samples, against needed shares of 0.494/0.503/0.500/0.447. Averaged over 5.33-10 ms it is 0.30/0.32/0.38/0.37. At G0 it is only 0.065, so it is gain-dependent like the refusal. So the triangle bound excludes slow states (>~10 ms; >30 ms comfortably) but is marginal and cannot exclude input dependence between 5.3 and ~10 ms (it exceeds the requirement only at G7.5; a single 1 ms frame of 4 realizations x 48 samples with +-3 dB frame-to-frame jitter). Suggested wording: 'refuted for any state or memory slower than ~10 ms; input dependence between 5.3 and ~10 ms is neither excluded nor supported by this bound.' A longer Hammerstein FIR does not capture that dependence: H5 with 1024 taps (21 ms) moves 0.8026 -> 0.8008 (take 20) and 0.7473 -> 0.7404 (take 7). If it matters, it is in a non-Hammerstein, likely pre-nonlinearity form (memory, not a tube slow state), consistent with leads 2/3 (WH cascade ~13 ms, hp300 prefilter). The tube slow-state mechanism stays refuted. VL3 is no counter-evidence: Laguerre size 8, pole 0.9, effective memory about 3 ms.

claims_to_downgrade.claim: 'Removing a component of relative RMS s lowers capacity by at most s' (triangle bound) as an airtight bound
claims_to_downgrade.reason: The arithmetic is correct and conservative in-sample: worst case c-0.3 = 0.45-0.50, orthogonal case 0.68-0.74. Interaction with the nonlinearity is included as long as s is defined as the full output difference caused by the state, which the model-free p1-p3 measures. Two caveats. (1) Fit on A, read on B: the residual changes by ||s_B - Phi_B theta(s_A)||, which can reach about 2||s||. Slow-state conclusions still hold (2x0.041 -> capacity >= 0.72; 10-30 ms: 0.80 - 2x0.19 = 0.42 > 0.3). (2) The measured s comes from one contrast (silence -> stationary multisine at -30/-24/-18 dBFS RMS). On B, 25.5% of 50 ms windows exceed -18 dBFS and the 99th percentile is -12.5 dBFS, so the DI drives the device beyond the loudest multisine. Representativeness of s for DI playing is supposed, not established.

claims_to_downgrade.claim: S1 calibration: 'The LPV family does not resolve a known state (S1-S0 only 0.010-0.017)'

The data are consistent with full capture as well as with none. Say 'the S1-S0 gap cannot discriminate capture from no capture', not 'does not resolve'. This rests on taking the multisine share as S1's DI share, which is itself not established.

claims_to_downgrade.reason: The steps stage measures only frame power relative to the segment's late power. A state that changes waveform or harmonic balance at constant level (bias shift) is invisible to it. It bounds the state's effect on output level, not its share of the output RMS.
